a2-unit-07.07.1 Urgent care:
Narrator: Dialogue one.
Doctor: Who's next? Oh no! What's happened to you?
Tom: I've just slipped on the ice outside my building. My foot really hurts. Have I broken it?
Doctor: Let me check. When did it happen?
Tom: About an hour ago. I was on my way to school.
Doctor: OK, good news. You haven't broken your foot, but you've sprained your ankle. Put some ice on it and rest for a few days.
Tom: Ice? I've had enough ice for today!
Narrator: Dialogue two.
Doctor: That doesn't look good! What have you done to yourself?
Lucy: I've just fallen off my bike. A car door opened right in front of me.
Doctor: Can I touch your arm?
Lucy: Ouch! That really hurts!
Doctor: I'm sorry. I think you've broken it. And you've hit your head too. Were you wearing a helmet?
Lucy: Yes, I was. Thank goodness!
Doctor: Good. We need an X-ray of that arm.
Narrator: Dialogue three.
Doctor: Hello. How can I help you?
Kate: Well, we've had a bit of an accident in my bakery.
Doctor: Both of you?
Rita: Yes. She's burned her hand, and I've cut my finger.
Doctor: Oh dear. How did that happen?
Kate: I forgot the tray in the oven was hot, and I touched it. When I screamed, Rita dropped a glass bowl!
Doctor: You haven't been very lucky today. Let's clean that cut and look at that burn.
